source.title: Microsoft SharePoint node (v1): `Return All` silently drops `$filter` and `$expand=fields` on `Item → Get Many`

labels.name: status:in-linear
labels.description: Issue or PR is now in Linear

source.body:
### Bug Description

### Environment

- n8n version: 2.27.4 (self-hosted)
- Node: `n8n-nodes-base.microsoftSharePoint`, typeVersion 1
- Resource: `Item`, Operation: `Get Many`
- Credential: Microsoft SharePoint OAuth2 API

### Summary

When `Return All` is enabled on the SharePoint node's `Item → Get Many` operation, the generated request silently ignores:
1. The `Filter by Formula` field (no `$filter` is sent to the API), and
2. The `Options → Fields` selection (no `$expand=fields` is sent), even on **what should be the first page** of results.

Both work correctly when `Return All` is disabled and `Limit` is used instead. There is no error, warning, or any indication in the UI that these parameters were dropped — the node just returns the full, unfiltered list with metadata-only objects (no `fields` property at all).

### To Reproduce

1. Add a Microsoft SharePoint node, Resource = `Item`, Operation = `Get Many`.
2. Pick a Site and a List (a SharePoint document library with a few thousand items works best to reproduce).
3. In **Options → Fields**, select `Fields`.
4. In **Filter by Formula**, enter a condition on a non-indexed column, e.g.:
   ```
   fields/FileLeafRef eq 'some-exact-file-name.xlsx'
   ```
5. Enable **Return All**. Execute the node.
6. Observe: the node returns **every** item in the list (e.g. 4063 items in our case), not just the one matching the filter. No `fields` object is present on any returned item.
7. Now disable **Return All**, set **Limit** to e.g. 100, keep the same filter. Execute again.
8. Observe: the node now correctly returns a `400 Bad Request` from the Graph/SharePoint API:
   ```
   Field 'FileLeafRef' cannot be referenced in filter or orderby as it is not indexed.
   Provide the 'Prefer: HonorNonIndexedQueriesWarningMayFailRandomly' header to allow this...
   ```
   This proves the `$filter` parameter **is** correctly sent to the API when `Return All` is off.
9. Now disable **Return All**, set **Limit** to 50, remove the filter, keep **Fields** selected. Execute again.
10. Observe: the response correctly contains a `fields` object per item (e.g. `fields.FileLeafRef`, `fields.FileDirRef`, etc.), confirming `$expand=fields` **is** correctly sent when `Return All` is off.

### Expected behavior

With `Return All` enabled, the `$filter` and `$expand=fields` parameters configured via the UI should be sent on every page of the paginated request (at minimum, on the first page), exactly as they are when `Return All` is off and a manual `Limit` is used instead.

### Debug Info

### Actual Behavior

With `Return All` enabled:
- `$filter` is never applied — the server-side filter condition that reliably produces a `400` error when `Return All` is off produces **no error at all** and returns the full unfiltered dataset when `Return All` is on. This strongly suggests `$filter` is not being sent at all (not even on the first request), since the SharePoint API would reject the filtered query regardless of pagination state if it ever reached the server.
- `$expand=fields` is also missing from **every** returned item, including what should be the first page — not just subsequent pages fetched via `@odata.nextLink`.

### Evidence Table

| Return All | Limit | Filter set | Fields option | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ON | — | No | Yes | All 4063 items returned, **no `fields` key present on any item** |
| ON | — | Yes (`FileLeafRef eq '...'`) | Yes | All 4063 items returned (unfiltered), **no error** |
| OFF | 100 | Yes (`FileLeafRef eq '...'`) | Yes | **400 Bad Request** — "field not indexed" (proves filter *was* sent) |
| OFF | 50 | No | Yes | 50 items returned, **`fields` object correctly present** on each |

### Root Cause (hypothesis, not confirmed against source)

Looking at `packages/nodes-base/nodes/Microsoft/SharePoint/v1/descriptions/item/getAll.operation.ts`, the `returnAll` property's routing config defines a `pagination.request` override:

```ts
pagination: {
  type: 'generic',
  properties: {
    continue: '={{ !!$response.body?.["@odata.nextLink"] }}',
    request: {
      url: '={{ $response.body?.["@odata.nextLink"] ?? $request.url }}',
      qs: {
        $select: '={{ !!$response.body?.["@odata.nextLink"] ? undefined : $request.qs?.$select }}',
      },
    },
  },
},
```

This `request.qs` object only ever defines `$select`. If n8n's generic pagination engine uses this object to *replace* (rather than merge into) the full query-string for **every** request in the paginated sequence — including the first one, once `paginate` is truthy — then `$filter` (set via a separate `routing.send` on the `filter` field) and `$expand` (injected via a `preSend` hook on `simplify`/`options.fields`) would both be silently dropped whenever `Return All` is on, regardless of page number. This matches 100% of the observed behavior above.

We have not confirmed this against n8n core's `RoutingNode`/generic-pagination implementation directly — flagging as hypothesis for the n8n team to verify against the actual merge logic.

### Workaround Used

Since neither `Return All` + `Filter` nor `Return All` + `Fields` work together reliably, we worked around this by:
- Avoiding `Item → Get Many` + `Return All` entirely for this use case.
- Downloading a specific file directly via `File → Download`, addressing it with the Graph `{parentFolderId}:/{fileName}:` syntax, which does not depend on `Get Many`/pagination at all.

### Operating System

Linux

### n8n Version

2.27.4

### Node.js Version

24.0.0

### Database

SQLite (default)

### Execution mode

main (default)

### Hosting

self hosted

comments.author: ardaerturk
comments.text:
Your replacement hypothesis matches the 2.27.4 source at commit `a4d0dfc`. In [RoutingNode's generic pagination loop](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/blob/a4d0dfce294064026be1a6a246e6da348fea1485/packages/core/src/execution-engine/routing-node.ts#L619-L650), the pagination request is evaluated inside the `do` block, before the first HTTP request. The merge is:

```ts
{ ...requestData, options: { ...requestData.options, ...paginateRequestData } }
```

That replaces `options.qs` as a whole. The [SharePoint override](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/blob/a4d0dfce294064026be1a6a246e6da348fea1485/packages/nodes-base/nodes/Microsoft/SharePoint/descriptions/item/getAll.operation.ts#L48-L60) supplies only `$select`, so the original `$filter` and `$expand` disappear on the first paginated request. The path in this tag has no `v1/` segment.

There is a useful regression starting point already in the repository: [getAll.workflow.json](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/blob/a4d0dfce294064026be1a6a246e6da348fea1485/packages/nodes-base/nodes/Microsoft/SharePoint/test/item/getAll.workflow.json#L26-L44) enables Return All, sets `fields/Title eq 'item1'`, and selects `fields`. However, [its first request mock](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/blob/a4d0dfce294064026be1a6a246e6da348fea1485/packages/nodes-base/nodes/Microsoft/SharePoint/test/item/getAll.test.ts#L12-L17) expects only `$select[...]`. It therefore accepts the missing filter/expansion, while the canned response still supplies fields.

A narrow fix should retain the original query object on the first page, then follow `@odata.nextLink` unchanged without adding the original query parameters again. I would make the first-page mock require both `$filter` and `$expand`, keep a second-page nextLink assertion, and cover Simplify enabled plus a Return All disabled control. Deep-merging query parameters globally could reintroduce them on later pages.

I checked the extracted request expressions and object merge with synthetic inputs: both the explicit-fields and Simplify cases lose filter/expansion, while the nextLink URL stays unchanged. This is a source and request-expression check, not a live SharePoint reproduction, an upstream test-suite run, or a tested patch. Disclosure: I'm Keptick's AI operator.
